main_diagnosis: The neg_avg_log_marginal_NLE of 22.3 remains high, suggesting systematic mismatch in stim-period distribution statistics (metrics 4–7) and possibly spike count (metric 1). The primary culprit is tau_z=500ms for IKM: this timescale is so slow relative to typical stimulus durations (~1–2 s) that z never reaches steady-state during stimulation, producing a drifting, non-stationary outward current rather than stable adaptation. Additionally, V_half_KM in [-50,-40] mV causes z≈8% at rest after 300ms pre-stim, creating a small but measurable resting outward current that can shift resting potential metrics (metrics 2–3). These two IKM design choices combine to corrupt multiple summary statistics simultaneously.

issues.description: tau_z=500ms is too slow relative to typical stimulus durations (~500ms–2s). During stimulation, z never converges to its per-voltage steady state; instead it drifts upward throughout the entire stimulus epoch, producing a non-stationary spike frequency adaptation that violates the tonic (regular, evenly-spaced) firing pattern expected in the data. This causes mismatch in spike count (metric 1), mean stim voltage (metric 4), and all higher-order distribution statistics (metrics 5–7) because the inter-spike voltage distribution changes progressively across the stimulus window rather than remaining stationary. A tau_z in the 100–250ms range would still far exceed typical ISIs (20–100ms), ensuring genuine cross-spike accumulation, while being short enough that z reaches near steady-state within the stimulus period and produces stable tonic firing.
issues.location: tau_z = 500.0 line; z[:,i] exponential Euler update in simulation loop
issues.suggestion: Reduce tau_z from 500ms to 150ms (e.g., tau_z=150.0). At tau_z=150ms: (a) 150ms >> typical ISI (20–100ms) → z still accumulates across spikes providing genuine SFA; (b) after ~450ms stimulation z reaches ~95% of z_ss → stationary tonic firing; (c) after 300ms pre-stim rest: z_rest ≈ z_inf(-65)*(1-exp(-300/150)) ≈ z_inf(-65)*0.865 — to compensate, shift V_half_KM range upward to [-40,-30] mV so z_inf(-65)≤0.076 and resting z≤0.066 (negligible resting I_KM). Update: V_half_KM = -40.0 + params[:,9]*(10.0/3000.0) for range [-40,-30] mV and decay_z = float(torch.exp(torch.tensor(-tstep/150.0, dtype=torch.float32))).

issues.description: V_half_KM range [-50,-40] mV combined with tau_z=500ms causes z≈8% at rest after 300ms pre-stimulus (z_inf(-65,V_half=-50)≈0.182; after 300ms: 0.182*(1-exp(-300/500))≈0.082). This produces a small but measurable resting I_KM that slightly hyperpolarizes the resting potential (metric 2) and adds an extra conductance term that reduces resting membrane resistance, compressing resting voltage fluctuations (metric 3 — resting V std). Even 8% resting z with gbar_KM~0.25 mS/cm² gives I_KM_rest ≈ 0.25*0.082*(−65+77) ≈ 0.25 μA/cm², which is non-negligible relative to the leak current and can systematically shift the inferred resting potential away from the experimental target.
issues.suggestion: Shift V_half_KM range from [-50,-40] mV to [-40,-30] mV by changing the offset: V_half_KM = -40.0 + params[:,9].float()*(10.0/3000.0). At the new lower bound V_half=-40: z_inf(-65)=1/(1+exp(2.5))≈0.076; z_inf(+30)≈0.999 (full AP activation unchanged). At the new upper bound V_half=-30: z_inf(-65)=1/(1+exp(3.5))≈0.029 [essentially silent at rest]. With tau_z reduced to 150ms, resting z after 300ms ≈ 0.076*0.865≈0.066 at worst — still small. This cleanly separates resting (near-silent IKM) from AP-period (fully-activated IKM) behavior and should restore accurate resting potential metrics.
